descriptions.title: Bilingual, region-driven SQLite spine
descriptions.body: The schema is the architecture. Every user-facing text field is a *_ja / *_en pair so the Japanese original is never lost while English is layered on top (Design Decision D4). Geography is a first-class reference table — all 47 prefectures with region group, climate, and an in_poc flag — so widening coverage is a data change, not a code change (D3). raw_listings holds the immutable scraped JSON keyed UNIQUE(source_id, source_listing_id) so a parser fix can re-derive listings without re-hitting the portal. listings carries the normalized, translated, deduped record with indexes on prefecture, price, type and dedup_key. SQLite runs in WAL with foreign keys enforced — adequate for a single-user local tool, and no server to operate.

descriptions.title: Adapter pattern: fixtures by default, live per portal
descriptions.body: Every source is a BaseAdapter subclass exposing fetch_raw(). When use_live_scraping=0 (the polite, offline POC default) it loads local JSON fixtures so the whole pipeline runs without touching the internet; when =1 it calls the portal-specific fetch_live(). Two portals — the at-home national Akiya Bank and SUUMO — have real selectolax scrapers (JIS-code per-prefecture URLs, section.propety / div.property_unit cards, polite rate-limited _get with a contact User-Agent). The other five adapters document their live selectors but still inherit fixture loading. A failing source is caught and skipped so it can never abort the whole ingest run.

descriptions.title: The ingest pipeline and cross-source dedup
descriptions.body: ingest() walks each enabled adapter: fetch_raw -> _store_raw (hash-guarded raw capture) -> normalize (derive era, seismic class, bedrooms, renovation estimate, and a bucketed dedup_key) -> translate (title now, description lazily) -> _upsert_listing. Upsert classifies every row as new / updated / duplicate / unchanged: the same raw capture updates only on content-hash change, and a listing sharing a dedup_key (prefecture + 5sqm-bucketed area + 100k-yen-bucketed price + address head) with an active listing from ANY source collapses to a duplicate. Only touched listing ids are then re-scored against profiles, so a re-run is cheap.

descriptions.title: Translation: free-first with a persistent cache
descriptions.body: translate() hashes the source text and checks the translations cache first — translate once, reuse forever, re-translate only when the source changes. On a miss it walks the configured engine order; 'auto' tries DeepL (if DEEPL_API_KEY is present), then a local Ollama model, then an offline real-estate glossary stub that does deterministic longest-match token replacement. This is the QI free-first principle in practice: with no paid key configured, all 187 current translations were produced locally by Ollama at zero marginal cost, and the stub guarantees the demo never breaks even fully offline.

descriptions.title: The matching engine — AND of specified constraints
descriptions.body: A Profile's criteria_json is a bag of optional constraints; a listing matches when it satisfies every constraint that is actually set (unspecified = no filter). Hard constraints (type, price with JPY/USD conversion, prefecture, region, land/building area, bedrooms, build year, seismic class, akiya-bank-only) gate the match; soft preferences (climate, keywords) only feed a 0..1 relevance score blended with price headroom (cheaper-vs-ceiling scores higher). A deliberate scout choice: akiya with NULL 'price on request' are never dropped by the price filter. match_for_listings scores on ingest; rematch_profile rebuilds one profile's matches on create/edit.

descriptions.title: Map, geocoding and hazard layers
descriptions.body: at-home detail pages carry no coordinates, so geocode.py resolves each distinct municipality once via OSM Nominatim (rate-limited to ~1/sec, cached in geocache) and applies a small deterministic jitter so several homes in one town don't stack on a single pixel. mapview.build_map() renders a folium choropleth of all 47 prefectures shaded by live listing count, highlights the focus corridor, and adds clustered price/photo pins. Base layers cover English labels, Japanese labels, GSI satellite and topographic maps, and four MLIT hazard overlays (flood, landslide, tsunami, storm surge) are toggleable for due-diligence.

descriptions.title: Scheduling without the heavy machinery
descriptions.body: The product spec floated Redis/Celery; for a single-user local tool that is overkill. scheduler.py uses one APScheduler BackgroundScheduler pinned to Asia/Tokyo: an interval job re-ingests and enriches every ingest_interval_hours (default 12), a daily 08:00 JST job digests houses added in the last 24h, and reload_profile_jobs registers one CronTrigger digest per enabled profile schedule (daily / weekly / monthly / custom 5-field cron). Digests bundle new matches into an on-site notification (read/unread tracked) and optionally email via local SMTP when email_enabled=1 and credentials are present.
